beats.narration: Same service name. Same interface. Signed build. Sharper English. Harbor Line has every familiar reason to call the replacement an upgrade. But should it inherit the Draft Notice service? Hold the evidence against Harbor Line's promise. Not yet. A service name says where requests go. Provenance says where an artifact came from. Neither shows that Harbor Line's promise survived.
beats.sync_anchor: should it inherit the Draft Notice service
beats.visual_purpose: Make familiar software continuity look persuasive, then expose the missing consumer promise.
beats.visual_action: Keep the DRAFT NOTICE nameplate fixed while OLD and NEW cartridges share an interface slot; stamp NEW with SIGNED and CLEARER, hold for the decision, then leave the contract aperture visibly empty.
beats.attention_target: the attractive candidate beside the still-empty promise aperture
beats.object_before: One old implementation occupies the Draft Notice route.
beats.object_after: A clearer signed candidate appears compatible, but the consumer promise remains untested.
beats.composition: Nameplate above two cartridges; empty gauge outline at right.
beats.motion_curve: Fast evidence stamps, then a guided comparison hold before the empty gauge is emphasized.
beats.camera_action: Static wide view that tightens once on the missing promise.
beats.hold_purpose: Let the viewer compare identity evidence with the absent consumer contract.
beats.visual_inference: Route, interface, provenance, and prose quality do not by themselves preserve the service promise.
beats.evidence_boundary: Harbor Line and both implementations are fictional teaching objects.

beats.narration: Build that promise into a capability gauge. It checks English and Spanish, keeps drafts private, blocks publication, expires old evidence, and leaves a receipt. The gauge belongs to Harbor Line, not to either model. This version-controlled promise is a Stable Capability Field. The old model fits. Its machinery may change, but a replacement inherits the service only where the required teeth still align.
beats.sync_anchor: The gauge belongs to Harbor Line
beats.visual_purpose: Externalize the stable object as a consumer-owned contract.
beats.visual_action: Assemble EN, ES, PRIVATE, ABSTAIN, EXPIRY, and RECEIPT teeth around the gauge; attach the route nameplate to it and slide OLD into an exact fit.
beats.attention_target: the gauge remaining fixed as the old cartridge enters
beats.object_before: The route name is the only apparent stable object.
beats.object_after: A versioned consumer-owned gauge defines the obligations implementations must fit.
beats.composition: Gauge centered, route nameplate above, cartridges staged left, history rail below.
beats.motion_curve: Teeth assemble one causal requirement at a time; OLD enters only after the contract is complete.
beats.camera_action: Tighten on tooth alignment, then return to the full gauge.
beats.hold_purpose: Make the field distinct from every implementation.
beats.visual_inference: The consumer contract, not the implementation slot, supplies stable capability identity.
beats.evidence_boundary: The gauge is a selected visual model, not a complete semantic checker.

beats.narration: Start with an English notice. Both models produce an acceptable private draft, and the replacement is clearer. On this one case, the upgrade looks obvious. Now send the Spanish case that once exposed a regression. The replacement refuses it. Then inspect its tool binding. The old model writes to the draft store. The replacement calls the publishing tool. Those failures point in opposite directions. One narrows who the service serves. The other widens what it may cause. Better writing does not cancel either change.
beats.sync_anchor: Those failures point in opposite directions
beats.visual_purpose: Show why one better output cannot cancel coverage loss or authority expansion.
beats.visual_action: Pass both cartridges through EN; jam NEW at ES; then route OLD to DRAFT STORE while NEW's PUBLISH tooth collides with the private outlet.
beats.attention_target: the missing Spanish fit and protruding publish tooth
beats.object_before: The candidate appears superior on one English draft.
beats.object_after: The candidate is clearer but narrows coverage and widens reachable effects.
beats.composition: Workload cards enter left; gauge center; private/publish outlets right.
beats.motion_curve: English clears smoothly; Spanish stops; the publish collision lands last.
beats.camera_action: Track each workload, then hold both failures in one frame.
beats.hold_purpose: Keep the two non-equivalent failures visible together.
beats.visual_inference: Output quality, population coverage, and authority are separate substitution obligations.
beats.evidence_boundary: The workloads and tool bindings are fictional counterexamples, not measured incidents.

beats.narration: A version label can signal an interface change. A signed build can bind the artifact to a history. Both matter, but neither proves that behavior, authority, and recovery stayed inside Harbor Line's promise. So the replacement receives a canary lease, not the default service. It may read approved sources and create private drafts for Harbor Line. A gate outside the model blocks publication. The lease expires, and the old model remains ready as fallback. The canary is bounded by consequence, not just traffic. One percent is not small when one call can publish, spend money, change durable state, or create descendants. The lease limits reachable effects as well as exposure.
beats.sync_anchor: bounded by consequence, not just traffic
beats.visual_purpose: Derive a useful canary decision from incomplete substitution evidence.
beats.visual_action: Attach VERSION and PROVENANCE seals without repairing failed teeth; close a CANARY sleeve around NEW with Harbor Line, PRIVATE, EXPIRY, and PUBLISH BLOCKED bands while OLD remains docked as fallback.
beats.attention_target: the effect-blocking sleeve and preserved old fallback
beats.object_before: Useful identity evidence coexists with material obligation failures.
beats.object_after: The candidate receives a consequence-bounded lease without inheriting default trust.
beats.composition: Candidate and sleeve center; blocked outlet right; fallback left; expiry on history rail.
beats.motion_curve: Seals attach respectfully, sleeve closes firmly, and a one-percent traffic ring expands into effect icons before stopping.
beats.camera_action: Widen from traffic percentage to the reachable-effect boundary.
beats.hold_purpose: Show that bounded use is a positive scoped decision, not candidate rejection.
beats.visual_inference: Canary scope must bound reachable consequences as well as request share.
beats.evidence_boundary: The lease design does not establish evaluator independence, enforcement, or successful fallback.

beats.narration: Suppose the Spanish failure is repaired and every private-draft check now passes. A city publisher asks to use the same service for live emergency notices. Does Harbor Line's lease transfer? Hold the lease against the changed use. No. The user, purpose, authority, consequence, and environment changed. That request needs its own field version and qualification. A new evaluator, tool, dependency, incident, or audience can also reopen an old decision. The field keeps each failed case beside the promise it tested. State and recovery duties follow the replacement into later reviews. Occupying the same slot erases nothing.
beats.visual_purpose: Test scoped transfer and preserve invalidation history.
beats.visual_action: Repair the ES tooth, then compare the Harbor Line lease bands with a CITY PUBLISHER / LIVE EMERGENCY card; mismatch consumer, purpose, authority, consequence, and environment, light invalidation pins, and retain failed cases on the history rail.
beats.attention_target: the changed-use bands refusing to align while history remains attached
beats.object_before: The repaired candidate appears ready to generalize beyond Harbor Line.
beats.object_after: The old lease remains useful but non-transferable to a materially different use.
beats.composition: Lease bands left, changed-use card right, history rail persistent below.
beats.motion_curve: ES repair lands first; bands compare during the guided hold; mismatches and invalidation pins appear after the answer.
beats.camera_action: Tighten on band comparison, then widen to the retained history.
beats.hold_purpose: Give the viewer time to compare scope bands before transfer is refused.
beats.visual_inference: Material changes in consumer, use, authority, consequence, environment, or evaluator reopen qualification.
beats.evidence_boundary: The changed-use case illustrates scoped qualification; it does not measure transfer risk.

beats.narration: A finite model can prove that selected replacements preserve an authored identity, do not widen authority, and carry the events the contract requires. Synthetic controls can expose known mismatches and lifecycle failures. But none of that proves real-world equivalence, independent evaluation, deployed enforcement, or reversal of external effects. The gauge is a disciplined boundary, not a certificate of sameness. It lets the machinery improve without silently moving the terms of trust. A replacement inherits the service only inside the scope its evidence actually supports.
beats.sync_anchor: a disciplined boundary, not a certificate of sameness
beats.visual_purpose: Separate the finite formal envelope from real replacement assurance and resolve the opening.
beats.visual_action: Enclose authored identity, no authority widening, required events, and synthetic controls inside a Lean boundary; keep equivalence, evaluator independence, enforcement, and effect reversal outside; return OLD DEFAULT and NEW CANARY beneath the fixed gauge.
beats.attention_target: the exact inside/outside proof boundary above the two scoped routes
beats.object_before: The gauge and controls could be mistaken for complete replacement assurance.
beats.object_after: Finite results remain useful inside their envelope while default inheritance stays limited to evidenced scope.
beats.composition: Finite envelope left; open-world obligations right; scoped routes and history below.
beats.motion_curve: Finite properties lock in sequence, open obligations remain unfilled, and the two route states settle under one unchanged promise.

beats.visual_inference: Finite contract consequences do not establish real equivalence, but they can prevent silent trust-term movement.
beats.evidence_boundary: No real-system equivalence, independent evaluation, deployed enforcement, recovery, safety, transfer, SOTA, AGI, or ASI result follows.
